content: [{"order":1,"type":"heading","text":"PostgreSQL Process Architecture and Memory Structures"},{"order":2,"type":"paragraph","text":"Understanding how PostgreSQL manages processes and memory is vital for database administrators and developers looking to optimize performance, troubleshoot bottlenecks, and ensure high availability."},{"order":3,"type":"subheading","text":"1. PostgreSQL Process Architecture"},{"order":4,"type":"paragraph","text":"PostgreSQL utilizes a multi-process architecture rather than a multi-threaded one. When you start a PostgreSQL cluster, a master process called the postmaster is initiated. This process oversees the entire database instance, manages incoming client connections, and spawns background processes."},{"order":5,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Postmaster: The primary coordinator process that listens on a network port, accepts connections, and starts backend worker processes."},{"order":6,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Backend Processes: Individual processes spawned for each connected client session to handle query execution."},{"order":7,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Background Worker Processes: Specialized utility processes such as the Checkpointer, WAL Writer, Background Writer, and Autovacuum Launcher."},{"order":8,"type":"code","text":"SELECT pid, usename, application_name, backend_type FROM pg_stat_activity;"},{"order":9,"type":"subheading","text":"2. Core Memory Structures"},{"order":10,"type":"paragraph","text":"PostgreSQL memory is broadly divided into two categories: Shared Memory (allocated when the server starts and shared across all processes) and Local Memory (allocated independently by each backend process for its specific operations)."},{"order":11,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Shared Buffers: The primary shared memory structure used to cache table and index data blocks in RAM."},{"order":12,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Write-Ahead Log (WAL) Buffers: Shared memory areas used to hold WAL data before it is flushed to disk."},{"order":13,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Work Mem: Local memory allocated per backend process for sorting and hashing operations before writing to temporary disk files."},{"order":14,"type":"bullet_point","text":"Maintenance Work Mem: Local memory used for heavy maintenance tasks like VACUUM, CREATE INDEX, and ALTER TABLE."},{"order":15,"type":"code","text":"SHOW shared_buffers;\nSHOW work_mem;\nSHOW maintenance_work_mem;"},{"order":16,"type":"subheading","text":"3. Best Practices for Memory Configuration"},{"order":17,"type":"paragraph","text":"Properly tuning shared_buffers and work_mem prevents excessive disk I/O and out-of-memory errors. Typically, shared_buffers is set to 25 percent of total system RAM, while work_mem must be adjusted carefully based on concurrency and available memory to prevent OOM killer interventions."}]
